complete_final_independent_report.report:
PASS for the restricted A–F statements, the complete supplied author argument, and target n4 with its full support n1–n3. The mathematical proofs are self-contained under the expressly permitted foundations. Original-P09 completion remains false; this audit changes no earlier verdict or completion count. No private artifacts, programmes, histories, or supplementary runtime observations were accessed.

Cofactor conventions and normalization (n1). Alternating multilinearity gives gamma^n=det(G)h^n. Differentiating det(G+sTheta) at s=0 gives tr(Theta C), where C=det(G)G^{-1} has the transposed signed-minor indices stated in n1. Consequently theta wedge gamma^(n-1)=tr(Theta C)h^n/n, including complex off-diagonal terms. C is positive Hermitian and det(C)=det(G)^(n-1). Conversely, for any positive Hermitian C, setting s=det(C)^(1/(n-1)) and G=sC^{-1} gives det(G)=s and det(G)G^{-1}=C; this also proves uniqueness. These identities transform by unitary conjugation and therefore hold globally without diagonalizing the test metric globally. Constant scaling by b multiplies every numerator and denominator by b^(n-1), preserves the Gauduchon equation, and gives the unique normalization b=A_h^(-1/(n-1)). Substitution of mu=(r/H)h^n yields the stated denominator formula. With Z=(H/n)C, normalization is integral tr(Z)dnu=1 and D_mu=nH^(-1/n) integral r^(1/n)det(Z)^(1/n)dnu. Compactness and positivity make R finite and positive.

A (n2). Constant rank supplies the smooth kernel and orthogonal-complement bundles. The spectral hypothesis gives B>=delta P_L. For Z>0, the block traces u=tr(P_K Z) and v=tr(P_L Z) are strictly positive, and tr(BZ)>=delta v by conjugating B-delta P_L with Z^(1/2). Thus t=integral v dnu satisfies 0<t<1, integral u dnu=1-t, and delta t<=e. In an adapted orthonormal basis, block elimination and completion of the square give det(Z)=det(U)det(V-W*U^{-1}W). The Schur complement is positive and at most V. Conjugation by V^(-1/2) proves its determinant is at most det(V); arithmetic-geometric mean on the two principal blocks then gives det(Z)<=(u/m)^m(v/q)^q. This explicitly controls the off-diagonal block rather than discarding nondiagonal tests. Applying weighted arithmetic-geometric mean to u/(1-t) and v/t, whose integrals against the probability nu both equal one, proves the required integrated determinant inequality. Finally, the logarithmic derivative of F(t)=((1-t)/m)^(m/n)(t/q)^(q/n) is (q-nt)/(nt(1-t)). Since t<=e/delta<=q/n, including the endpoint, replacement by e/delta is valid and gives exactly A. Dropping the factor (1-e/delta)^(m/n)<=1 gives the stated O(e^(q/n)) bound. No Gauduchon, constancy, or commutativity assumption enters this upper estimate.

B. For a normalized threshold-minimizing sequence under the separately established or assumed equality kappa=a, e_j=A_B(gamma_j)=A_alpha(gamma_j)-a is strictly positive and tends to zero. Eventually it lies in A's range, so D_mu<=K e_j^(q/n), with K=n(R/H)^(1/n)m^(-m/n)(delta q)^(-q/n). Positivity alpha>=a h establishes only kappa>=a. Neither the author proof nor n2 improperly infers equality or invokes general Gauduchon existence.

C and the geometric construction (n3). On the unit square torus, omega=(i/2)dz wedge dbar(z)=dx wedge dy has integral one. Its factor pullbacks are closed, have square zero, and commute as two-forms. Therefore mu is a probability volume, h^n=n!mu, H=n!, and r=R=1. Alpha is closed and alpha>=a h>0. Its actual, undivided top intersection is V=n!a^m(a+delta)^q. Nefness follows directly by choosing zero potential in the defining approximate-positivity condition. Bigness is witnessed directly by the smooth closed positive current alpha>=a h; no nef-bigness theorem is used. For a closed (1,1)-form beta, the distinct bidegrees in d beta=0 give partial beta=barpartial beta=0, hence D(beta^(n-1))=0 with the exact factor i/(2 pi). This verifies admissibility of all constructed closed metrics. The same exterior-power calculations hold for arbitrary positive unit-area factor forms; translation invariance describes the particular forms selected in the author proof.

D. For every e in (0,delta), put t=e/delta and choose C=(n/n!)diag(((1-t)/m)I_m,(t/q)I_q). Its entries are positive, and G=det(C)^(1/(n-1))C^{-1} defines the actual closed positive metric obtained by using these constant coefficients on the factor forms. The full inverse-cofactor identity established above applies; directly, its diagonal signed minors equal the prescribed entries of C and its off-diagonal minors vanish. The trace formulas give A_h=(n!/n)tr(C)=1 and A_B=(n!/n)delta tr(P_L C)=e. Its denominator equals (n!)^((n-1)/n)det(C)^(1/n), which simplifies to exactly n/(n!)^(1/n) times ((1-t)/m)^(m/n)(t/q)^(q/n). For every variable, nondiagonal normalized test, B=delta P_L makes t=e/delta exactly. The block and integrated inequalities therefore give this upper bound throughout the full interval, without A's monotonicity replacement. The displayed closed metrics attain it, so it is a maximum over all Gauduchon tests. Both endpoints are excluded by strict positivity of both block traces. The maximum tends to zero at either endpoint and has greatest value (n!)^(-1/n) at e=delta q/n. These checks cover all n>=2 and all permitted nonzero block dimensions.

The two infima. Positivity gives A_alpha/A_h>=a, while the actual normalized witnesses with t tending to zero give ratios a+delta t tending to a. Thus kappa=a, independently establishing B's antecedent in this example. For lambda, let A=diag(aI_m,(a+delta)I_q). Although AC need not be Hermitian, A^(1/2)CA^(1/2) is positive Hermitian, has trace tr(AC), and determinant det(A)det(C). Arithmetic-geometric mean therefore gives tr(AC)/n>=(det(A)det(C))^(1/n). Integration with the verified n! constants yields A_alpha>=V^(1/n)D_mu for every positive test. Gamma=alpha is closed and attains equality, with A_alpha(alpha)=V and D_mu(alpha)=V^((n-1)/n). Hence lambda=V^(1/n) over the entire Gauduchon class.

E and the additional calculus check (n4). Writing S=m/a+q/(a+delta), normalization of gamma=alpha gives excess delta q/((a+delta)S)=delta q a/(na+m delta), strictly between zero and delta q/n. Its normalized numerator is n/S=a+e_*. The derivative of the logarithm of the fixed-excess quotient (a+delta t)/M(t) is exactly ((na+m delta)t-qa)/(nt(1-t)(a+delta t)). It has its unique minimum at t=qa/(na+m delta), diverges at both endpoints, and the maximizing metric there is the normalized alpha. Every normalized threshold-minimizing sequence instead has e_j tending to zero and hence D_mu tending to zero. Its numerator tends to a>0, so its root-volume quotient actually tends to infinity. Only the excess tends to zero. Thus an antecedent requiring A_alpha tending to zero cannot hold here, and the example supplies no application or contradiction of a nonbig conditional theorem.

F and provenance. The explicit examples have threshold-minimizing sequences, and every such sequence has vanishing denominator. They therefore disprove universal availability of a positive limiting denominator on those sequences. Their explicit bigness and special-case root-volume calculation establish neither a counterexample to closed-nef positive-intersection bigness nor a solution of the general bridge or original P09. Statements that broader questions remain open are understood as the supplied scope restriction: this argument does not settle them. The bibliography snapshot URLs and their raw equivalents returned 404; their historical attribution is unverified, but no indispensable mathematical inference depends on those sources.

Define C=adj(G)=det(G)G^{-1}. Using indices 1,...,n, C_jk=(-1)^(j+k) det(G with row k and column j deleted). Thus C is the transpose of the signed-minor array. In dimension two it is [[G_22,-G_12],[-G_21,G_11]]. Its eigenvalues are det(G) divided by the positive eigenvalues of G, so C is positive Hermitian. No diagonality is assumed.

Differentiating the determinant by its multilinear expansion gives sum_jk Theta_jk C_kj=tr(Theta C). Therefore theta wedge gamma^(n-1)=tr(Theta C)h^n/n. In dimension two the mixed coefficient is Theta_11 G_22+Theta_22 G_11-Theta_12 G_21-Theta_21 G_12, verifying the complex off-diagonal contraction. Also det(C)=det(G)^(n-1).

[premiseIndex=1; additionalPremiseIndices=[0]] Given any positive Hermitian C, put d=det(C)>0 and s=d^(1/(n-1)), taking the positive real root. [premiseIndex=1; additionalPremiseIndices=[2]] In an orthonormal basis adapted to K and L write Z=[[U,W],[W*,V]]. The principal blocks U,V are positive. Block elimination gives det(Z)=det(U)det(S), where S=V-W*U^{-1}W. Completing the square in the quadratic form of Z proves S>0, while W*U^{-1}W>=0 gives S<=V. Thus the eigenvalues of V^(-1/2)SV^(-1/2) lie in (0,1], and det(S)<=det(V). Arithmetic-geometric mean on the positive eigenvalues of U and V gives det(Z)<=(u/m)^m(v/q)^q. [premiseIndex=1; additionalPremiseIndices=[0,2]] Let p=m/n and z=q/n. Apply arithmetic-geometric mean to m copies of x=u/(1-t) and q copies of y=v/t. It gives x^p y^z<=p x+z y. Combining this with the block determinant bound and n1 proves D_mu<=n(R/H)^(1/n)((1-t)/m)^(m/n)(t/q)^(q/n). Neither a Gauduchon equation nor an invariant-test restriction was used.

Consequently D_mu<=n(R/H)^(1/n)((1-e/delta)/m)^(m/n)((e/delta)/q)^(q/n), exactly A. The factor 1-e/delta is positive because q<n.
